abstract_check.evidence: The note abstract matches the primary abstract verbatim, including the source wording “more less-intense, or fewer more-intense partners.” The article’s abstract is not confused with an LLM-generated summary.

claim_checks.claim: Four strategies (strong/favour-few, medium, weak/favour-many, staged) use prior successful interaction history; staged moves from strong to weak/unknown alters.
claim_checks.evidence: §2.5; probabilities are delegated to earlier Sutcliffe & Wang work, and the note appropriately leaves the exact selection functions unspecified.

claim_checks.claim: Trust is directional, accumulates/decreases after response, and wanes; the prose and printed pseudocode differ.
claim_checks.evidence: §§2.3–2.6. The note preserves the conflicting §2.4 prose, §2.6 compression/waning pseudocode and §4.4 selected log-increase/linear-decrease setting; it does not claim an exact resolved transition equation.

claim_checks.claim: Fitness equations and basic selection setup.
claim_checks.evidence: §4.2 PDF p.4 shows WB=((sum of ego-to-alter trust)×incoming interactions/outgoing interactions)/number of ties and R=forage turns×number of ties. Note equations match. §4.3 confirms lifetime 2000, N=300, equal strategies, weighted fitness ranks, removal of bottom 20% and replacement by random copies of top 20%.

claim_checks.claim: Baseline evolutionary parameters and strategy outcomes.
claim_checks.evidence: §§4.4–4.11: log increase/linear decrease, MC=10, waning=.08, 20 generations; FM and R:WB are experimental controls; best SBH fit at FM=1:4 and R:WB=1:3 in this experiment, with the paper separately noting best total 150 ties only at FM=1:3.

claim_checks.claim: Kin, defection, heritable genes, crossover/mutation and outcomes.
claim_checks.evidence: §§4.12–4.15 and 5.1–5.8 support the note’s parent/sibling kin carry-over, five-kin substitution and larger-seed effects, defection trends, three four-allele genes, 0.9 crossover, random-gene recombination, 0.01 mutation, parameter ranges, and stochastic wellbeing/resource results. Note describes thresholds as experiment-dependent.

Abstract and §§6.3–6.10; note frames findings as simulation outcomes, distinguishes wellbeing from resource fitness, and states that the model is ego-network based, omits spatial effects, and does not use prior defections for partner selection.

bibliography_check.evidence: The count and ordering correspond to the source list, but the note uses compact opaque identifiers as link labels (e.g. IsFriendshipAkinToKinship; SmallGroupsAsComplexSystemsFormationCoordinationDevelopmentAndAdaptation) rather than source-verified natural titles. A workspace search found no corresponding targets for representative compact identifiers. Thus 62/62 item count does not establish title/target integrity; convert to verified source titles and existing note targets where available.

source_metadata_check.evidence: The primary publisher header gives JASSS 15(4), article 3, Published 31-Oct-2012 and DOI 10.18564/jasss.2059; note metadata matches.

coverage_scope: Full primary source (not abstract-only), including equations and all bibliography entries.
unresolved_or_conflicting_source_details: The source itself conflicts on trust decreases/compression/waning and selects a different increase/decrease setting in §4.4; note discloses this and avoids resolving it.
The source refers detailed partner-selection/trust functions to Sutcliffe & Wang (2012); those are intentionally not inferred as exact formulas here.
The source equations do not define zero-tie or zero-outgoing handling; the note explicitly discloses this.

latest_reaudit.claim_reaudit: PASS: corrected four FM genotypes (8:1, 5:1, 4:1, 1:1), response-defection genotypes (0.01, 0.025, 0.05, 0.075), and source-compatible genotype/crossover/mutation summaries. Fitness equations, model controls, outcome boundaries, abstract, and source-conflict disclosures remain supported.

bibliography_check.evidence: The newly added title-bearing aliases materially improve the bibliography. One alias still does not match the primary source: note reference “A social identity model for deindividuation phenomena” differs from the source title “A social identity model for deindividualisation phenomena” (JASSS source text line 856; Reicher, Spears & Postmes 1995). Correct the natural title alias while retaining whichever target path is appropriate. Other title aliases and the count/order checked appear consistent. This leaves 61/62 title labels verified.

other_source_conflicts: The trust description in §2.4 says plus/minus one and logarithmic compression, while §2.6 pseudocode gives MaxCR-CI×Trust and W waning; §4.4 selects log increase/linear decrease. Current note faithfully discloses the conflicts and does not select one implementation.
Exact trust/waning and alter-selection functions are inherited/referred to another paper and remain unspecified.
Zero ties/outgoing interactions are not defined by source equations; note discloses this.

The source misspells Reicher et al. as “deindividualisation”; the note uses the canonical title “A Social Identity Model of Deindividuation Phenomena,” checked against the work’s publisher/DOI record per source correction review.
